##### feat: vc-x1 commit, install, and run-dev opening

The cycle's setup commit: create and publish the bookmark at `main`, move the Todo entry into this
block, and bump the version-of-record. Under the bend above it keeps the package name, installs
under `--root tmp/dev` from both validate lists, and removes the `build.rs` guard, so the cycle
runs on the convention it introduces. It also carries the Todo's own split, made before the
opening: the code entry cut from **agent-files(proposal): v0.3.1** and placed first.

##### feat: an install table in the config

The config gains `[install] release`, `dev`, and `dev-bin`, the schema's stale examples are fixed
and the model regenerated, `README.md`'s single-name section becomes the dev root's, and two
validate runs show one binary left under `tmp/dev`.

* Nothing reads the new keys yet.
  - The schema names the subcommands that will, `install`, `install --dev`, and `run-dev`, so its
    prose is ahead of the binary until their rungs land. On this rung's tree the keys are valid
    config and nothing more: the dev binary's `validate-config` finds no problem, since its schema
    is built from the same file, while the installed `0.85.5` reports the three keys and their
    links as unknown until Land.
* The two-run check passed on the cycle's own rungs.
  - The opening's full run installed `0.85.6-0` under `tmp/dev`, this rung's installed `0.85.6-1`,
    and after it `tmp/dev/bin` holds one `vc-x1`, its `-V` the second version, with
    `.crates.toml` and `.crates2.json` rewritten to name it alone. Nothing was deleted between.
* The README still described the guard and the old fixture path.
  - Its Build and install section now says the name never changes and where a cycle's builds go,
    and its Acceptance fixtures section says `.fixtures`, that the tests are ignored without
    `--include-ignored`, and that an absent fixture panics naming the build command.

##### feat: validate-desc takes -s, the first scope

The scope leaf and the resolver, and their first user, a read-only command: `-s w|a|b` required,
whose commits are checked, one table per side under its label, `-s p` refused, and `-R` optional,
where.

* The scope leaf knew sides, not a plain repo.
  - `RepoScope` is a `Scope` or `Por`, parsed from the four forms long or short, and `parse_scope`
    learned the short forms too, so the read commands accept `-s a` ahead of the sweep. The comma
    forms stay with `parse_scope`, for the read commands that predate `both`.
* Nothing resolved "which repos" for a required scope.
  - `resolve_scoped_repos` is that: the sides from the workspace the start is in, by its root or
    either repo, and for `p` the start itself, refused when it is a side. A repo under a
    workspace's tree that is neither side is plain, so a scratch repo in `tmp/` is reachable.
* `validate-desc` checked one repo, `-R`'s, against its partner.
  - It checks each scoped side against its other side, `b` being both directions, and refuses
    `p` at params time with the reason. The init test that ran it once per side runs `-s b` once
    per workspace.
* The rule was tried where a wrong resolution costs nothing.
  - The write half, `sync` and `squash-push` on the same resolver, was written first and set
    aside on the local bookmark `wip-sync-squash-push`, the next rung, so this one publishes
    nothing by the new rule before the rule has been seen working on a read.
  - One impurity of the path split: `common.rs` carries the two messages that now say
    `squash-push -s a`, one rung before squash-push takes it.

##### feat: vc-x1 commit makes the rung's commit pair

A rung becomes a pair of local commits, one per repo, each stamped with the other's change id,
before any push, so the description review is of the commit itself and the lookup works on an
unpushed rung.

* The pair's two ids were going to be one known and one predicted.
  - Both are read from the working copies before either commit is made, since a jj commit keeps
    `@`'s change id, so the work commit's trailer names the agent `@` and the agent commit's the
    work `@`, each written once. A test checks the ids survive the commits and that validate-desc
    passes the pair in both directions with nothing pushed.
* The pair can be made in two steps.
  - `-s w` makes the work commit now, its trailer naming the agent `@` all the same, and leaves
    the agent half to push, which commits the journal as the partner, wink's thought at this
    rung's review: it works with the installed push today, and the review's own transcript lands
    in the rung's agent commit. `-s b` makes both now, `-s p` a plain repo's commit, and only
    `-s a` is refused, an agent commit made first being the one unpaired case. `--title` and
    `--body` are required and may not be blank, `--body @PATH` reads a file, and the editor path
    push has is left out until it is asked for.
* The work `@` is a decision, the agent `@` a journal.
  - An empty work `@` is nothing to commit and refuses before anything is touched, while the agent
    `@` is committed as it stands. A failure after the first commit restores both repos from `jj
    op` snapshots, push's rule inside its mutation window.
* The resolver called a single-repo workspace a side.
  - `FixturePor` lays out a work config with no agent, and `-s p` on it was refused as "the work
    side of the dual workspace". A side is one only when the config declares an agent, so a
    single-repo workspace is plain for `p`, with the resolver's test covering it.
* This rung is the first made by its own command.
  - `tmp/dev/bin/vc-x1 commit -s w` made it, the body from `tmp/body.md`, and the installed
    `vc-x1 0.85.5 push` published it, committing the agent journal as the partner, since its work
    half was already there. `-s b` waits for the push rung: handed both commits, today's push
    makes the journal a second agent commit.

##### feat: vc-x1 push only publishes the pair

Push carries no description: its agent half folds the journal into the pair's agent commit when
`@-` already names the work commit, else commits the journal as the partner with the work
commit's description, its work half refuses unsquashed work, and it publishes the pair as
reviewed. The transcript's push lines keep being recognized by the lookup in both the old form
and the new.

* Push wrote descriptions and ran gates of its own.
  - The review gate, the message stage, the editor, `--title`, `--body`, and `--no-squash-push`
    are gone, and the retired flags are errors naming themselves. What remains is `-s`, `-R`, the
    bookmark as a check, `--dry-run`, and `--step` with `--yes` for its gates. A rerun stays safe,
    since every stage still checks its precondition.
* The pair can arrive in three states.
  - A `plan` stage reads them before anything is touched: the agent `@-` names the work commit
    (`commit -s b`) and the journal folds into it at squash-push, the agent `@` is the change the
    work commit names (`commit -s w`) and the journal is committed as the partner with the work
    commit's own text, or the agent repo changed since the commit and the unpublished work commit
    is restamped to name the agent `@`, said out loud, a published one refusing. Each state has a
    test, the restamp's keeping the work change id.
* The refusals had to come before any mutation.
  - Reading the agent `@` snapshots it, so a journal file the size limit refuses stops the plan
    with the file named and no rollback, the m-10-0 case now a CLI test of `commit -s b` for
    either side and of `push -s b` for the journal.
* The halves and the plain repo.
  - `-s w` publishes the work commit alone, `-s a` completes the agent half after it, the by-hand
    remainder of a run that stopped past push-work, and `-s p` publishes a plain repo's `@-` on
    its bookmark with no trailer asked for. The bookmark is the line's unless named, and a name
    that is not among the nearest bookmarks below `@-` is refused naming them.
* The lookup knew push lines by two fixed prefixes.
  - It knows `commit` as a third verb, since the body now rides on it, and the binary by its
    basename after any path, since this cycle's rungs run `tmp/dev/bin/vc-x1`. The fixture's
    recorded lines still read as before.
* The pair's two paths and the two-repo snapshots were written twice.
  - `pair.rs` holds `Pair`, `resolve_pair`, and `Snapshots` with `take` and `restore`, the pieces
    `commit` and `push` both had, wink's question at this rung's review. The description helper
    went to `desc_helpers`, where the trailer's shape lives, and the one-off pieces, the body's
    `@PATH`, the partner check, the preflights, stay where they are until a third copy appears.
* Two tests and a script still spoke the old push.
  - The sync CLI test's peer push is `commit -s w` then `push -s w`, and `with_trailer` in
    `desc_helpers` is the one place a trailer is appended, fixing the double blank line commit
    left. `support/fixtures/build-dr-1.py` still drives `push --title --body` and is the
    **dr-1 is built in Rust** cycle's to retire, so a rebuild of the fixture after Land needs it
    changed first.

##### feat: vc-x1 squash folds work into the pair

A review's fix folds into the pair in both repos at once, refusing a published side, and a
description fix goes the same way with the trailers restamped.

The first rung under the two-paragraph body, wink's (2026-10-20), so this subsection is the full
account its body points at.

* A rung could not be continued once committed.
  - `vc-x1 squash -s b` folds the work `@` into the work commit and the journal into the agent
    commit, each keeping its change id, so both trailers stay right untouched. `-s w` and `-s a`
    fold one side, `-s p` a plain repo's `@` into its `@-`.
* The agent side can be committed, pending, or changed.
  - A partner committed by `commit -s b` takes the journal. A pending one, after `commit -s w`,
    is the journal already, push's to commit with the work commit's text, so squash leaves it,
    and a changed one is push's to restamp. A test covers the first two.
* A description fix was a re-describe the rules forbid by hand.
  - `--title` with `--body` rewrites the descriptions and keeps each trailer, the sanctioned
    re-describe, never of a published commit. A test checks the pair still validates in both
    directions.
* A published side is a remote rewrite.
  - It is refused before anything moves, as is a work `@-` with no trailer. A failure after the
    first mutation restores both repos from the shared snapshots.
* The pair's state was read by push alone.
  - `pair.rs` gained `work_commit`, `partner`, `refuse_conflicts`, and `is_published`, which push
    and squash share, and `desc_helpers::read_body` is the `@PATH` reading commit and squash
    share. The third copy of the conflict check, squash's, is what moved it.
* The lookup did not know squash.
  - `squash` is a verb beside `commit`, `push`, and `squash-push`, since it carries a body.
* Push's plan said the agent half twice, wink's question at this rung's push dry run.
  - The decision line and the summary line are one: what is published, then what the agent half
    does and why, the restamp still a warning. Folded into this rung by its own `squash -s b`,
    the first real fold, after the commit.
* Commit and squash mutated with no preview, wink's point at this rung's review.
  - Both take the shared `--dry-run` leaf: `commit --dry-run` prints the descriptions it would
    write, trailers included, so a description is reviewed before anything is committed, and
    `squash --dry-run` prints what it would fold and re-describe. A test of each checks nothing
    moved.

##### fix: push runs the agent half, then the work half

Push bundled its two halves into one mutation window and logged them out of order, though each
commit's trailer is fixed before push runs, so neither half needs the other. `push -s b` is now
`push -s a` then `push -s w`, each with its own rollback, in the order the pair is completed.

* The halves shared one mutation window and one rollback.
  - The agent half completes the partner by the state found, then squash-pushes `main`. The work
    half restamps if its trailer does not name the partner, then sets and pushes the bookmark.
    Each takes a one-repo `pair::Snapshot` of the repo it touches and restores only that one, since
    the other may have moved on, a journal writing to it.
* The restamp was decided from the agent side, before the agent half ran.
  - It is the work half's question, "does my trailer name the partner?", asked after the agent
    half, so it holds for every order, `-s a` then `-s w` included, which a test now covers. A
    published work commit that would need it is refused before the agent half publishes.
* The plan was a stage of its own with a line of its own.
  - Each half's first line says what it does and why, `push agent:` then `push work:`, in the
    order they run, and the work bookmark is resolved first, so a run that cannot publish the work
    half stops before the agent half publishes anything.
  - In a dry run the intent lines carry `[dry-run]` like the step lines, wink's catch at this
    rung's push dry run, where "push work: publish ..." read as done. Folded in by `squash -s b`.

##### feat: sync and squash-push take -s, required

The two write commands this cycle changes rather than builds take the resolver: `-s` required,
`-R` optional, `squash-push` acting on each resolved repo, work before agent, and the README and
the messages saying `-s a`. Written before the validate-desc rung and held on
`wip-sync-squash-push` until it.

* Sync and squash-push guessed which repos they acted on.
  - Both take `-s`, required, and `-R`, optional, by `resolve_scoped_repos`. A bare `sync` was
    the repo it ran in, and a bare `squash-push` the cwd's repo, so the workspace's other repo was
    silently left out. `squash-push` acts on each resolved repo, work before agent, so `-s b` is
    the fold-and-publish of both that asks nothing, and `-s a` is wink's daily
    `squash-push -R .agent-session/`.
* The README, three messages, and the support script named `-R <bot-repo>`.
  - They say `-s a`, the README's sync section states the rule once for every scoped command,
    and its squash-push examples carry the scope.
* The stash was written against the resolver's first name.
  - Brought onto the pushed tip by a rebase and a squash into `@`, with no conflict, its two uses
    of `resolve_write_repos` renamed, and its bookmark deleted once empty.
* After Land, wink's `squash-push -R .agent-session/` and the agent-files' `sync --scope=both`
  are the old forms.
  - The first fails naming `--scope`, the second still parses, and both are v0.3.1's text to
    change, its "The scope flags in the rules" item.
* `-s p` on a side is refused for sync and squash-push too.
  - On those two it would act as the side's own scope, but on commit, push, and squash it would
    bypass the pair, so the one rule stays, wink's call at this rung's review (2026-10-20): `p`
    is a repo with no partner, and the error names the side's scope.

##### feat: squash-push takes --dry-run

Squash-push was the one write command with no preview: `--dry-run` prints what it found and what
it would do in each resolved repo, and changes nothing.

* `squash-push --dry-run -s a` was refused as an unknown flag.
  - It takes the shared `DryRunFlag` leaf and stops after its precheck, which has already printed
    the verdict line, naming each step it would take: the squash, or that the source is empty and
    it would skip it, the bookmark set, and the push. With `-s b` it says so for each repo, work
    first. A test checks the tail stays in `@` and `main` does not move.
* Push's agent half builds squash-push's params directly.
  - It passes `dry_run: false`, since push's own dry run stops before it.

##### feat: vc-x1 merge, and commit --closing on it

The closing is made as the merge of the trunk and the ladder when it is committed, so no reshape
follows its review, by a primitive that adds any sources to any mutable commit's parents.

* Making a commit and giving it several parents are separate operations, wink's point at this
  rung's review.
  - `vc-x1 merge -s w --target <rev> --from <revset>...` adds the sources to one target's
    parents, after the ones it has, keeping its change, description, and change id. One target,
    empty or not, and N sources, no assumption about where either lives, wink's model
    (2026-10-20): two lines of work merged into one commit, ten commits on one bookmark or many
    merged into it one at a time, a root as a source. All three flags are required.
  - Merge is an implied add, and each `--from` a revset of one or more commits, wink's call at
    review. The first form replaced the parent list, so the second of ten merged one at a time
    had to repeat the first. Each revset's commits are added oldest first, a source already a
    parent is skipped, and a merge adding nothing changes nothing. jj-lib's `rebase_commit` takes
    the whole parent list, so all the sources go in one call and one jj op, the same tree a loop
    of one-at-a-time merges gives. Removing a parent is not a merge, and `jj undo` or `jj rebase
    -r` does it.
* Keeping the target's tree and swapping its parents is right for one ladder only.
  - The first version did that, and with several sources the merge would have silently reverted
    all but one. The verb has jj's rebase meaning, the new tree the merge of the sources with the
    target's own change, which a test of two sources checks.
* Limits that are not artificial.
  - Refused: a source at or below the target, a cycle, a revset naming no commit, and a target in
    jj's `immutable()` unless `--ignore-immutable`, as `jj` refuses it, wink's call at review.
    The first form refused a published target, `::remote_bookmarks()`, which counts a rung pushed
    to its cycle bookmark, though jj counts it mutable and the push after its rewrite takes
    approval anyway. vc-x1 evaluates revsets in-process, so the session config now carries the
    jj CLI's revset aliases, `trunk()` and `immutable()` among them, and every layer's
    `[revset-aliases]`, the user's `immutable_heads()` included, override them as in `jj`.
  - The git backend holds no merge with the root as a parent, jj's own refusal, so merging into
    a commit that sits on the root fails and the snapshot restores the repo.
  - Reported and allowed: a conflicted result, left conflicted as jj leaves it, push refusing a
    conflicted repo anyway. A source that is an ancestor of another was going to be warned about
    as redundant, until the dogfood dry run of a closing warned: `main` below the last rung is
    the no-fast-forward shape a closing is, so it is unremarked.
    `-s a` and `-s b` are refused, the agent repo never holding a merge.
* The name, wink's: "reparent" read as an operation on one commit's parent, and "trapezoid" names
  only some results, a closing on one rung being a triangle. `merge` names the result.
* `commit --closing` sets `@`'s parents to `main` and the last rung, then commits.
  - It sets them by the primitive `merge` uses, not by `merge`'s append, which would put the
    trunk second. It merges before committing, so `@`'s parents are set and the commit keeps
    them, and `main`
    is the current one, not the fork point, so a `main` that moved during the cycle is joined by
    the merge rather than needing a rebase first, which a test checks. The title's " closing"
    suffix is checked against the flag both ways, and with no ladder, a single-step cycle, a
    " closing" title is just a title and `--closing` is refused.
  - A test makes the closing on a ladder of two rungs and folds a review fix into it with
    `squash`, which keeps both parents.
* Dry runs.
  - `commit --closing --dry-run` says which commits the closing would join, and `merge
    --dry-run` the sources it would add and the parents that would make.

##### feat: vc-x1 move-bookmark repositions a bookmark

A bookmark is put in position before it is pushed, by a command of its own, since push only ever
sets the line's bookmark to `@-`.

* Push cannot name its target, the question that raised the rung, wink's (2026-10-20).
  - Push's work half sets the line's bookmark to the work `@-`, and its BOOKMARK argument is only
    a check, a name that must be among the nearest bookmarks below `@-`. Its agent half sets the
    agent-repo's `main` to the partner. Both ends are pinned, so a bookmark anywhere else is put
    there first, by a verb that only repositions, and push keeps its form.
* `vc-x1 move-bookmark -s w --bookmark NAME --target REV` is `jj bookmark set NAME -r REV`.
  - All three flags are required, wink's. The bookmark must already exist, none being created,
    and the target is a revset of exactly one commit, a bookmark or a rev, the form `merge`'s
    `--target` has. A bookmark already at the target is left alone.
  - Nothing is pushed, so every remote change still goes through push and its approval.
* The checks vc-x1 adds to jj's.
  - A move backward or sideways, leaving commits off the bookmark's line, is refused unless
    `--allow-backwards`, the flag and the refusal `jj bookmark set` has. Forward means every
    commit the bookmark points at, a conflicted bookmark's several included, is an ancestor of
    the target.
  - `-s a` and `-s b` take `--yes`, wink's at review, the first form having refused them, since
    the agent-repo's `main` is otherwise push's agent half's to set. Each repo of the scope moves
    the same name, the target resolved in it, `@-` in each, and every repo is checked before any
    moves, so a bookmark or a target missing from one stops both, which a test checks. A failure
    of a later move restores the repos already moved from their snapshots.
  - `-s p` takes the repo from `-R`, required, as it is, wink's at review: none of the
    workspace's checks, so it moves a bookmark in either side of a dual workspace or any jj repo,
    and careful use is the user's. The bookmark, target, and direction checks stay, wink's pick.
  - No trailer is asked of the target, and no immutability, since a bookmark's move rewrites no
    commit: `main` moved to the closing merge at Land is the case it serves next.
* Dry run.
  - `--dry-run` says where the bookmark would move from and to, and moves nothing.

##### feat: vc-x1 install promotes main

The promotion is a subcommand that checks it is installing pushed `main` at a bare version, the
check the `build.rs` guard the opening removed could not make, and `--dev` is the dev install on
demand.

##### feat: vc-x1 run-dev runs the dev binary

The dev binary, off the PATH, is run through the config, with a warning when it is not the
manifest's version.

##### feat: vc-x1 commit, install, and run-dev closing

Closing out the cycle.

# Cycle model

A cycle's `## In Progress` block, shown as a specimen rather than a skeleton: the `config loader`
cycle, mid-run, with its opening landed and its first work rung current. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [The In Progress block](notes.md#the-in-progress-block).

One thing the specimen cannot show:

- a single-step cycle drops both bookends and all the steps are in the one commit: the ladder is one
  unlinked rung with the bare title, and there are no rung subsections under it ([Cycle
  shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).

## In Progress

### refactor: extract config loader

#### Problem

Config parsing lives inside the CLI entry point, so every subcommand that wants a setting reaches
through `main` for it, and a test cannot load a config without building the CLI.

#### Solution

Move config loading into its own module with a single `load` entry point that the CLI and the tests
call alike.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a new test that loads a config from a fixture file without touching `main`,
and `vc-x1 config --validate` reports the same findings as before the move.

#### Deliberation

- one work rung, not two: the parser and the loader were going to be split first and moved second,
  but the move is what forces the split, so doing them together is fewer edits
- the acceptance check compares `config --validate` output rather than asserting on internals, so a
  later rename inside the module does not invalidate it

#### Ladder

- [refactor: extract config loader opening][1] (done)
- [refactor: split loader from parser][2] (current)
- [refactor: extract config loader closing][3]

##### refactor: extract config loader opening

The cycle's setup commit: create and publish the bookmark, delete `## Closed`'s contents, move the
Todo entry into this block, and bump the version-of-record.

##### refactor: split loader from parser

Loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load without parsing and a test cannot parse
without a file on disk.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config/loader.rs` finds and reads the file, returning the text and its path, so a caller that
    only wants to know which file was read stops here.
  - `config/parser.rs` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands it a string and never
    touches the filesystem.
    - the error type stays shared for now, since splitting it would change the messages
      `config --validate` prints and the acceptance check compares them
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field access moves behind the module
    boundary and the CLI no longer knows the file's shape.

##### refactor: extract config loader closing

Closing out the cycle.

# References

[1]: #refactor-extract-config-loader-opening
[2]: #refactor-split-loader-from-parser
[3]: #refactor-extract-config-loader-closing

34	## In Progress
35	
36	### feat: vc-x1 commit, install, and run-dev
37	
38	(wink + agent, 2026-10-20, opened 2026-10-20) The code **agent-files(proposal): v0.3.1** names: a
39	rung is committed locally before it is pushed, the closing is made as its trapezoid, the dev build
40	installs under its own root, and the promotion is a subcommand.
41	
42	#### Problem
43	
44	What the user reviews is not what is published. A rung's commit exists only once `vc-x1 push` has
45	made and published it, so a fix after the review of its description is a remote rewrite and a
46	squash-push in both repos. The closing is changed twice more after its review, at Land: the
47	package's plain name is squashed back into it, and the trapezoid recipe reshapes it into the merge.
48	The rename exists because a mid-cycle `cargo install` would otherwise replace the consumers'
49	binary, and Land's promotion itself names no command.
50	
51	#### Solution
52	
53	Provisional, the Todo's plan as filed:
54	
55	- An `[install]` table in the config: `release`, the promotion,
56	  `["cargo install --path . --locked"]` here, `dev`, the dev install,
57	  `["cargo install --path . --locked --root tmp/dev"]` here, both lists like `[validate]`'s, and
58	  `dev-bin`, the dev install's binary, `"tmp/dev/bin/vc-x1"` here. `.vc-config.md`'s
59	  `[validate] full` ends with the dev install's line. The stale `vc-config.md` examples are fixed
60	  with the keys, fast's `["cargo test --bins"]`, full's `cargo test` without
61	  `-- --include-ignored`, and `test.fixtures`' `"../vc-x1-fixtures"` with its "skips with a notice"
62	  prose, and `vc-config-model.md` is regenerated.
63	- A scope resolver shared by `commit`, `squash`, `push`, `squash-push`, and `sync`: `-s`, required,
64	  one of `work|w`, `agent|a`, `both|b`, or `por|p`, a plain repo with no pair, and `-R` optional,
65	  the workspace by its root or either repo for `w|a|b`, the repo itself for `p`, the cwd without
66	  it. No `-s` is an error naming the four. `-s p` on a repo that is one side of a dual workspace is
67	  an error naming the side, and `-s w|a|b` on a directory with no workspace config is one.
68	- `vc-x1 commit -s b` makes the rung's commit pair from the two working copies, each stamped with
69	  the other's change id, with the given title and body. `-s w` and `-s a` are errors in a dual
70	  workspace, since a half is an unpaired commit, and `-s p` commits a plain repo with no trailer.
71	- `vc-x1 squash` folds each scoped working copy into its side of the pair, the review's fix into
72	  the work commit and the review's transcript into the agent commit, and refuses a side whose
73	  commit is published. With `--title` and `--body` it rewrites both descriptions and restamps the
74	  trailers, the one sanctioned re-describe of a trailer-carrying commit.
75	- `vc-x1 push` only publishes: the work bookmark `@-` sits on, and the agent-repo's `main`. Its
76	  agent half folds the agent `@` first, the journal's last lines, and its work half refuses a
77	  non-empty `@`, which is a `squash` or the next rung, the user's call. `--title`, `--body`, and the
78	  bookmark argument go, the bookmark inferred from `@-` and named only as a check.
79	- `vc-x1 squash-push` stays, wink's most-used command, `squash-push -s a` the agent half of a push
80	  on its own, and `-s w|b` the fold-and-publish that asks nothing.
81	- `vc-x1 merge -s w --target <rev> --from <revset>...` adds the sources to one target's parents,
82	  with jj's rebase meaning, refusing a target in jj's `immutable()` unless `--ignore-immutable`.
83	  `vc-x1 commit -s b --closing` sets `@`'s parents to `main` and the last rung and then commits:
84	  the closing as the merge close-out, its first parent the current `main`, its second the last
85	  rung. The " closing" and " dead-end closing" title suffixes are checked against the flag, never
86	  its trigger.
87	- `vc-x1 move-bookmark -s w --bookmark NAME --target REV` moves an existing bookmark to one
88	  commit, locally, and never pushes, `-s a|b` with `--yes`, and `-s p` in the `-R` repo with no
89	  workspace checks. Push is unchanged.
90	- `vc-x1 install` runs `[install] release` after checking that `@-` is `main` at `main@origin`,
91	  `@` is empty, and the version is bare, and `vc-x1 install --dev` runs `[install] dev` with no
92	  check, the mid-cycle refresh of the dev binary.
93	- `vc-x1 run-dev` runs `[install] dev-bin` with the given arguments from any directory of the
94	  workspace, and warns when the binary's `-V` is not the manifest's version.
95	
96	#### Acceptance check
97	
98	In a scratch dual workspace made by the dev binary's `init`: `commit -s b` makes a pair whose
99	trailers name each other, a `squash -s b` after a further edit in each repo folds both and leaves
100	the trailers valid, `push -s b` publishes the pair unchanged and refuses while the work `@` holds
101	an edit, and each of the five commands without `-s` exits non-zero naming the four scopes.
102	`commit -s b --closing` on a bookmark of two rungs makes a merge whose parents are the fork point
103	and the second rung, and a `squash -s b` into it keeps both. On a plain jj repo, `commit -s p` and
104	`push -s p` commit and publish with no trailer.
105	`install` refuses, or warns, when `@-` is not `main` at `main@origin`, and `install --dev` leaves
106	`tmp/dev/bin/vc-x1` at the manifest's version. `run-dev -V` prints the manifest's version. In this
107	workspace, two full `validate` runs at different versions leave one binary under `tmp/dev`, its
108	`-V` the second version, and `tmp/dev/.crates2.json` naming it.
109	
110	#### Deliberation
111	
112	- Multi-step, a trapezoid the default, the agent's proposal and wink's go at the bookmark, eight
113	  rungs then, fourteen since the pair, the read-first scope, push's halves, squash-push's dry
114	  run, and move-bookmark (2026-10-20): opening, the install table, validate-desc with the
115	  resolver, the commit pair, push publishing only, squash, push's halves, sync and squash-push,
116	  squash-push's dry run, the closing as the merge, move-bookmark, install, run-dev, closing.
117	  - The install table is first, so every later rung's validation installs under `tmp/dev`.
118	  - The resolver is ahead of the commands that take it, and the commit rungs come before install
119	    and run-dev, being the larger change. The closing as the merge is its own rung, so the plain
120	    pair is reviewed before the merge builds on it.
121	- No rename, a bend of Opening step 6 and Land step 1, wink's say at the opening's review
122	  (2026-10-20): the cycle dogfoods its own change, so the opening keeps the name `vc-x1`, moves
123	  the two validate lines to `--root tmp/dev`, and removes the `build.rs` guard, which would refuse
124	  the suffixed version under the plain name on every cargo verb. The bend covers this cycle's
125	  pushes and its Land, which restores no name, and nothing else: the rule's text is v0.3.1's to
126	  change.
127	  - What the opening's validate run left behind before the bend, a `vc-x1-dev 0.85.6-0` in
128	    `~/.cargo/bin`, is wink's to remove.
129	  - `README.md`'s single-name section describes the guard that is gone, and the install table
130	    rung rewrites it with the `[install]` keys it describes.
131	- The code runs ahead of the rules, as its own cycle: the rule text names commands, so the
132	  commands exist before the rules do. This cycle's own rungs are pushed by the installed
133	  `vc-x1 0.85.5`, with `--title` and `--body`, and the next cycle runs on what this one lands.
134	- One dev root, `tmp/dev`, not one per version, wink's suggestion weighed and set aside: the
135	  version is in the binary, `cargo install --path` always rebuilds and overwrites, and a directory
136	  per rung is the litter `versioning.md` Dev artifact name warns of.
137	  - The one stale case is a failed install leaving the previous rung's binary, which `run-dev`'s
138	    `-V` check names.
139	- `install --dev` exists from the start, wink's vote (2026-10-20): fast is `cargo test --bins`
140	  alone, so only a full run refreshes `tmp/dev`, and a refresh on demand needs no full run.
141	  - The dev install's line is written twice, in `[install] dev` and at the end of `[validate]
142	    full`, until the installed `vc-x1` has the subcommand and full's last entry can be
143	    `vc-x1 install --dev`.
144	- The guard moves from `build.rs` into `vc-x1 install`: a build script sees every cargo verb but
145	  not an install's root, so once the dev build carries the plain name it cannot tell a dev install
146	  from the promotion, while `vc-x1 install` sees the bookmark, the remote, and the version.
147	  - A hand-typed `cargo install --path .` stays unguarded, a slip the sanctioned path never makes.
148	  - Open: whether a failed check refuses or warns.
149	- `commit` makes both repos' commits, wink's direction (2026-10-20) that every rung be local like
150	  the closing, taken one step further: the plan had commit make the work commit and push make the
151	  agent commit, with the trailer stamped from a predicted change id and checked at push. With the
152	  pair made together both ids are known, nothing is predicted, and push carries no description at
153	  all, so the reviewed text cannot be replaced on the way out.
154	  - The review's transcript is in the agent `@` when push runs, so push's agent half folds it into
155	    the pair's agent commit first, a squash into an unpublished commit, which keeps its change id.
156	    A `squash-push -s a` between commit and push publishes the agent half early, and push finds it
157	    done.
158	- `squash` exists because a rung is continued, wink's point: a review's fix must fold into the
159	  pair, and `jj squash` by hand does one repo and knows nothing of the other. It refuses a
160	  published side, and when the agent half went out early it folds the work side alone and says
161	  the transcript goes with the next rung, where it would land today.
162	  - A description fix is a re-describe, which the rule forbids by hand on a trailer-carrying
163	    commit, and the pair carries trailers from the start. `squash --title --body` is the way, so
164	    the rule's text becomes never by hand and never on a published commit, v0.3.1's to write.
165	- The two working copies mean different things, which is where push and squash-push part: the
166	  agent `@` is a journal, never empty while a session runs, and folding it is never a decision, so
167	  push's agent half always folds it. The work `@` is a decision, a fix or the next rung, so push
168	  refuses it and `squash-push -s w|b` is the user saying fold it and go.
169	- `-s` is required and `-R` optional, wink's rule (2026-10-20), after `--por` was weighed as the
170	  alternative for a plain repo and retired into the scope `p`: a write command never guesses which
171	  repos it acts on, `sync`'s "neither flag means the repo I am in" being fine for a look and not
172	  for a commit, where a silent half is an unpaired commit. `-R` is then only ever where, and `-s`
173	  which. The short names `a`, `w`, `b`, `p` are wink's, `squash-push -s a` replacing today's
174	  `squash-push -R .agent-session/`.
175	  - The same rule for every command that touches a repo, the read commands' defaults, the validate
176	    family, and clone's and init's `--por`, is the sweep **every repo command takes -s, required**
177	    in `TODO.md`, kept out of this cycle so the ladder stays on its subject.
178	  - To check at the push rung: the lookup recognizes push invocations in transcripts by their
179	    command text, and the fixture's recorded lines are the old form, so the new form must be
180	    recognized without the old one being lost.
181	- A read-only command takes the scope first, wink's suggestion at the write rung's review
182	  (2026-10-20): `validate-desc -s b` shows the resolver working, with nothing published if the
183	  resolution is wrong, and it is a check that would be run anyway. The write rung, already
184	  written, was split by path into the resolver half, which the validate-desc rung builds on, and
185	  the `sync` and `squash-push` half, a local commit on `wip-sync-squash-push` that follows later.
186	  The resolver lost its `write` name on the way.
187	- `-s w` is the pair in two steps, wink's thought at the commit rung's review (2026-10-20): the
188	  refusal of `w` as "unpaired" was wrong, since the agent `@`'s id is known at that moment just as

194	  (2026-10-20): the halves are independent, since each trailer is fixed before push runs, so
195	  `push -s b` is `push -s a`, mirroring the `commit -s w` before it, then `push -s w`. Its own
196	  rung rather than a fold into the squash rung, since it rewrites push's structure and the squash
197	  rung was reviewed, and the squash rung went out by the old push.
198	- `squash-push --dry-run` is a rung inserted after the stash, wink's pick (2026-10-20), when
199	  `squash-push --dry-run -s a` was refused as an unknown flag: the other write commands all had

# Cycle model

A cycle's `## In Progress` block, shown as a specimen rather than a skeleton: the `config loader`
cycle, mid-run, with its opening landed and its first work rung current. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [The In Progress block](notes.md#the-in-progress-block).

One thing the specimen cannot show:

- a single-step cycle drops both bookends and all the steps are in the one commit: the ladder is one
  unlinked rung with the bare title, and there are no rung subsections under it ([Cycle
  shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).

## In Progress

### refactor: extract config loader

#### Problem

Config parsing lives inside the CLI entry point, so every subcommand that wants a setting reaches
through `main` for it, and a test cannot load a config without building the CLI.

#### Solution

Move config loading into its own module with a single `load` entry point that the CLI and the tests
call alike.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a new test that loads a config from a fixture file without touching `main`,
and `vc-x1 config --validate` reports the same findings as before the move.

#### Deliberation

- one work rung, not two: the parser and the loader were going to be split first and moved second,
  but the move is what forces the split, so doing them together is fewer edits
- the acceptance check compares `config --validate` output rather than asserting on internals, so a
  later rename inside the module does not invalidate it

#### Ladder

- [refactor: extract config loader opening][1] (done)
- [refactor: split loader from parser][2] (current)
- [refactor: extract config loader closing][3]

##### refactor: extract config loader opening

The cycle's setup commit: create and publish the bookmark, delete `## Closed`'s contents, move the
Todo entry into this block, and bump the version-of-record.

##### refactor: split loader from parser

Loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load without parsing and a test cannot parse
without a file on disk.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config/loader.rs` finds and reads the file, returning the text and its path, so a caller that
    only wants to know which file was read stops here.
  - `config/parser.rs` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands it a string and never
    touches the filesystem.
    - the error type stays shared for now, since splitting it would change the messages
      `config --validate` prints and the acceptance check compares them
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field access moves behind the module
    boundary and the CLI no longer knows the file's shape.

##### refactor: extract config loader closing

Closing out the cycle.

# References

[1]: #refactor-extract-config-loader-opening
[2]: #refactor-split-loader-from-parser
[3]: #refactor-extract-config-loader-closing

81	project's record, and the payload ships it as a skeleton: `## In Progress` reading
82	`_No cycle currently in progress._`, the other sections empty.
83	
84	An entry is a `###` heading, its title, followed by its text. Priority is file order, the first
85	entry the highest, and reprioritizing is moving the entry. The title is unique within its file and
86	is the entry's anchor, so a citation is a link, `[title](TODO.md#<slug>)`, that the anchor check
87	verifies ([Prose form](prose.md#prose-form) for the text). Entries carry no number: a rank number
88	renumbers on every move and every citation that holds one goes stale, which is why the numbered
89	form was retired (2026-08-27). An entry's sub-entries, when it groups several, are bullets with a
90	bold title, cited by the bold text.
91

93	
94	```
95	## Todo
96	
97	### Add new feature X
98	
99	The feature, in a sentence or two ([details](features.md#feature-x)).
100	
101	### Fix bug Y
102	
103	What is wrong and where [[1]].
104	
105	[1]: bugs.md#bug-y
106	```

108	## The In Progress block
109	
110	A cycle's record, `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, written at the opening
111	([Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)), finalized and moved to `## Closed` by the closing commit, and
112	deleted by the next opening ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)). The picked-up `## Todo`
113	item is moved here (never copied) and becomes the cycle-record's **provisional items**, all
114	required, all revised as rungs land. The title is a heading one level below `## In Progress` and the
115	other five are headings one level below the title (a plain cycle: `###` title, `####` items, and
116	under a program heading, each one deeper):
117	
118	- **title**, the cycle's name, what `git log --grep` finds it by
119	- **problem statement**: what is wrong, a sentence or two
120	- **solution statement**: what will be done about it, broad. Provisional, and the close-out's commit
121	  body carries the final one
122	- **acceptance check**: the measure of "are you finished?", specific enough that a reader can run
123	  it. Not the per-commit validation, which asks whether the artifact still works. A changed check is
124	  one of the things the deliberation exists to justify
125	- **deliberation**: how the other five were decided, one bullet per decision. The bullet's lead
126	  names the decision and its sentence states it, and the sub-bullets carry the reasons, the
127	  alternatives weighed, and the costs accepted, so a reader can skim the decisions and read the
128	  reasons only where they doubt one. `_None._` when there was nothing to deliberate, which is a real
129	  answer
130	- **ladder**: one rung per step, `- [<title>][M]` plus `(current)` / `(done)`, with `[M]: #<slug>`
131	  in the file's `# References`. The markers stay when the block moves to `## Closed`. `<title>` is
132	  the rung's commit title, `<type>: <desc>` per
133	  [Conventional-commit shape](prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit), so a moved
134	  `## Todo` entry is retitled. The closing rung, `<cycle title> closing`, is linked like the rest
135

137	the rung's exact title, so the ladder is their index. Each opens at laddering with an abstract-sized
138	intent statement (the rung's problem and solution in a sentence or two) and completes at the rung's
139	landing with the conceptual delta: design points, consequences, deferrals, never a restatement of
140	the landed commit body. The closing rung's opens with the stub "Closing out the cycle." and
141	completes at close-out with what closing taught, in problem/solution form, or `_None._`.
142	
143	A rung is `- [<title>][M] (marker)` and carries no detail beyond that: the title links to the rung's
144	subsection. A step is identified by its title (prose.md's [Steps are named, not
145	numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)), so a title carries no number, no version, and no
146	SHA. The version-of-record still bumps for every rung and its suffix still encodes the stage, but
147	that encoding belongs to the manifest and appears nowhere in prose.
148	
149	A single-step cycle's ladder is one unlinked rung, `- <cycle title> (marker)`, with no subsection
150	under it: a subsection headed by the title would collide with the title heading's anchor ([Cycle
151	shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).
152	
153	The block is the cycle's only record. A design finding that must outlive the cycle goes into a
154	`notes/` file by the rung that made it ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).

1:# Versioning
8:## Terms
21:## A stamp, not a name
29:## Advancing X.Y.Z: patch by default
43:## Grammar and storage
81:## Recording the version-of-record
102:## Dev artifact name
128:## Unique per commit (preference, not requirement)
139:## Suffix scheme
176:## Agent-files version
---
    goal, none stating a problem of its own, and each opened one would leave the others citing an
    entry that is gone.
  - The opening was pushed and its agent-repo commit's `ochid:` trailer names it, so the cycle
    closes and lands rather than being dropped with its bookmark, the case the dead-end item of
    **agent-files(proposal): v0.3.1** was filed for.
  - Re-describing the opening as the first layer's was weighed and set aside: the agent-repo's
    opening would keep the old title, an exception to record, where a dead end bends nothing.
- Rust, not Python, wink's call: no dependency the project does not otherwise have, and Windows
  and macOS in view.
  - The Windows and macOS points are design intent until a CI run on them checks it: line
    endings, symlinks, path shapes, case-insensitive filesystems.
- Built by the tests, not by `build.rs`: a build script cannot tell `cargo test` from
  `cargo install`, runs before the crate it would need is compiled, and sees only
  build-dependencies.
- A fresh temp dir per test run, not a cached `.fixtures/dr-1`: the build is deterministic and
  took about two seconds under Python, so caching buys little and costs a version stamp, a
  build-then-rename, and a race between concurrent runs.
- Every user asks, no gate test, wink's point: a gate named to sort first is fragile, and every
  `dr1_*` test already asks through `dr1()`, so whichever asks first builds. What is given up is
  only an earlier stop.
- The failure stops the run, wink's ask: fail fast, front and center.
  - Prototyped 2026-10-19 in a scratch crate: the banner showed through the output capture, a
    running test was cut off, and a filtered run that needs no fixture was untouched.
  - The `ctor` crate's before-main hook was weighed and set aside: a new dependency, jj-lib run
    before the runtime is fully set up, and a build even for filtered runs.
- Fixtures that cannot be generated, such as the real-history ladder **lookup is tested on a
  reordered ladder** wants, stay with **Fixtures are named by their source**: fetched, and an
  absent one a loud stop with the remedy.
- Unseeded, decided at the plan rung: change ids differ per build, which the generated
  relationships file absorbs, and byte-reproducibility is out of reach anyway, since the
  transcripts carry the build directory's absolute paths.
- The jj CLI stays for the builder's repo operations, a deviation from the solution as filed,
  which said no `jj` or `git` would be involved. The record is the truth the lookup tests check
  lookup against, and lookup is built on jj-lib, so the record is read with the CLI. The tests
  already need it, and git runs only as jj's own push subprocess, which jj-lib needs too. What goes
  is `python3` and the installed `vc-x1`.
- The in-process calls get their chosen time and committer, and no signing, from a test-only
  override of one thread's jj settings, since a test may not write the process's environment and
  in-process jj-lib otherwise reads the developer's jj config, signing key included. Found at the
  plan rung's review, when a sandbox hid the key and a test's in-process `init` failed to sign.
- The record is kept in `zDOING.md` per the trial that file describes, and the ladder's labels
  start at `[0]`, continuing the local experiment the last cycle began.

#### Ladder

- [test: the tests build the dr-1 fixture opening][0] (done)
- [test: the tests build the dr-1 fixture dead-end closing][1] (done)

##### test: the tests build the dr-1 fixture opening

The cycle's setup commit: create and publish the bookmark at `main`, move the Todo entry into this
block, bump the version-of-record, and rename the package to `vc-x1-dev`.

##### test: the tests build the dr-1 fixture dead-end closing

Closing out the cycle as a dead end, the first under the dead-end item of
**agent-files(proposal): v0.3.1**. What closing taught:

* A dead end's title says so.
  - The closing is the cycle title plus " dead-end closing", wink's rule for
    **agent-files(proposal): v0.3.1**, run here ahead of it. By the same rule the title cap does
    not bind the suffix, so this title's 55 characters stand.
* The plan rung leaves no commit.
  - It was never pushed, so the ladder is the opening and this closing. Its one lasting product,
    `notes/fixture-dr-1.md`, lands here, and its subsection, the port mapped against the Python
    builder, survives only in the agent-repo's transcript.
* Version: the closing carries `0.85.5`, and Land releases it, since `main` gains the note and the
  Todo entries. Whether a dead end should release nothing stays open in **agent-files(proposal):
  v0.3.1**.
* Close-out shape: trapezoid, the dead-end form, reshaped at Land. The closing becomes the merge
  on `main`, so the opening stays reachable through its second parent and its agent-repo trailer
  resolves.

content.content:
60	## Todo format
61	
62	`TODO.md` has these sections, in this order. Each item in them is a short description with
63	reference links to more detail.
64	
65	- `## Continuation notes`: where the agent was, for the agent that comes next. Ephemeral, never a
66	  record, `_None._` by default, written before a restart or a loss of context, and reset by the
67	  agent that reads it, after filing each fact into its home or keeping the bullet whose fact has
68	  none, so a reset never destroys the only copy of anything.
69	- `## In Progress`: the running cycle's record ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).
70	- `## Waiting`: important work that cannot start yet. Each entry names what it waits on and its
71	  rank once unblocked, and every opening checks the conditions.
72	- `## Todo`: entries in priority order, the first highest. The long-tail backlog is in
73	  [todo-backlog.md](../notes/todo-backlog.md).
74	- `## Ideas`: unranked.
75	- `## Bugs`: a pointer to [bugs.md](../notes/bugs.md).
76	- `## Closed`: the last cycle's finished record.
77	- `# References`: the file-local reference definitions, the file's last section ([Reference
78	  numbering](#reference-numbering)).
79	
80	Every adopter has one `TODO.md` of this shape. It is not an agent-file, since its content is the
81	project's record, and the payload ships it as a skeleton: `## In Progress` reading
82	`_No cycle currently in progress._`, the other sections empty.
83	
84	An entry is a `###` heading, its title, followed by its text. Priority is file order, the first
85	entry the highest, and reprioritizing is moving the entry. The title is unique within its file and
86	is the entry's anchor, so a citation is a link, `[title](TODO.md#<slug>)`, that the anchor check
87	verifies ([Prose form](prose.md#prose-form) for the text). Entries carry no number: a rank number
88	renumbers on every move and every citation that holds one goes stale, which is why the numbered
89	form was retired (2026-08-27). An entry's sub-entries, when it groups several, are bullets with a
90	bold title, cited by the bold text.
91	
92	Example shape:
93	
94	```
95	## Todo
96	
97	### Add new feature X
98	
99	The feature, in a sentence or two ([details](features.md#feature-x)).
100	
101	### Fix bug Y
102	
103	What is wrong and where [[1]].
104	
105	[1]: bugs.md#bug-y
106	```
107	
108	## The In Progress block
109	
110	A cycle's record, `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, written at the opening
111	([Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)), finalized and moved to `## Closed` by the closing commit, and
112	deleted by the next opening ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)). The picked-up `## Todo`
113	item is moved here (never copied) and becomes the cycle-record's **provisional items**, all
114	required, all revised as rungs land. The title is a heading one level below `## In Progress` and the
115	other five are headings one level below the title (a plain cycle: `###` title, `####` items, and
116	under a program heading, each one deeper):
117	
118	- **title**, the cycle's name, what `git log --grep` finds it by
119	- **problem statement**: what is wrong, a sentence or two
120	- **solution statement**: what will be done about it, broad. Provisional, and the close-out's commit
121	  body carries the final one
122	- **acceptance check**: the measure of "are you finished?", specific enough that a reader can run
123	  it. Not the per-commit validation, which asks whether the artifact still works. A changed check is
124	  one of the things the deliberation exists to justify
125	- **deliberation**: how the other five were decided, one bullet per decision. The bullet's lead
126	  names the decision and its sentence states it, and the sub-bullets carry the reasons, the
127	  alternatives weighed, and the costs accepted, so a reader can skim the decisions and read the
128	  reasons only where they doubt one. `_None._` when there was nothing to deliberate, which is a real
129	  answer
130	- **ladder**: one rung per step, `- [<title>][M]` plus `(current)` / `(done)`, with `[M]: #<slug>`
131	  in the file's `# References`. The markers stay when the block moves to `## Closed`. `<title>` is
132	  the rung's commit title, `<type>: <desc>` per
133	  [Conventional-commit shape](prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit), so a moved
134	  `## Todo` entry is retitled. The closing rung, `<cycle title> closing`, is linked like the rest
135	
136	The ladder heads the **rung subsections**, one per rung under it, the closing included, headed by
137	the rung's exact title, so the ladder is their index. Each opens at laddering with an abstract-sized
138	intent statement (the rung's problem and solution in a sentence or two) and completes at the rung's
139	landing with the conceptual delta: design points, consequences, deferrals, never a restatement of
140	the landed commit body. The closing rung's opens with the stub "Closing out the cycle." and
141	completes at close-out with what closing taught, in problem/solution form, or `_None._`.
142	
143	A rung is `- [<title>][M] (marker)` and carries no detail beyond that: the title links to the rung's
144	subsection. A step is identified by its title (prose.md's [Steps are named, not
145	numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)), so a title carries no number, no version, and no
146	SHA. The version-of-record still bumps for every rung and its suffix still encodes the stage, but
147	that encoding belongs to the manifest and appears nowhere in prose.
148	
149	A single-step cycle's ladder is one unlinked rung, `- <cycle title> (marker)`, with no subsection
150	under it: a subsection headed by the title would collide with the title heading's anchor ([Cycle
151	shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).
152	
153	The block is the cycle's only record. A design finding that must outlive the cycle goes into a
154	`notes/` file by the rung that made it ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).
155

0	# Notes
1	
2	This directory contains various notes and documentation related to the project. Each file is
3	organized by topic for easy reference.

## Suffix scheme

The cycle (opening -> commits -> closing, per the [Cycle protocol](../AGENTS.md#cycle-protocol))
encodes each commit's phase in the version suffix, the **final identifier `0` marking a
Preparation**.

This is the manifest's own spelling, read by whoever inspects `Cargo.toml` or `-V` output. It is not
a name for a step: a step is identified by its title, and an in-flight ladder rung carries neither a
number nor a version (see [Steps are named, not numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)).
The identifiers below count commits within a phase, and nothing dereferences one.

- `X.Y.Z-0`: Preparation
- `X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, ...: the commits between
- `X.Y.Z`: Close-out (bare version, no suffix)

**Preparation is optional.** A lightweight cycle, with no ladder and no setup commit, skips `-0` and
starts at `-1` (its first commit). A single-step cycle is one commit, the Close-out, and carries the
bare `X.Y.Z` ([Cycle shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)). The same holds at every level: a sub-cycle
needing no Preparation omits its `.0` (see Nesting). One that grows a Preparation later adds the `0`
step without renumbering siblings.

Disambiguation:

- `-10`: commit #10 (final identifier `10`), not a Preparation.
- `-1.0`: Preparation of the `-1` sub-cycle (final identifier `0`).

**Nesting.** Sub-cycles append another level, recursively:

- `X.Y.Z-3.0`: Preparation of the `-3` sub-cycle
- `X.Y.Z-3.1`, `X.Y.Z-3.2`: its commits between
- `X.Y.Z-3`: its Close-out
- `X.Y.Z-3.1.0`: Preparation of the `-3.1` sub-sub-cycle

Bump the version-of-record at the start of every step (the per-commit checklist carries the step),
so the manifest always records the commit it will be part of and, per the preference above, every
commit carries a distinct version.

139	## Suffix scheme
140	
141	The cycle (opening -> commits -> closing, per the [Cycle protocol](../AGENTS.md#cycle-protocol))
142	encodes each commit's phase in the version suffix, the **final identifier `0` marking a
143	Preparation**.
144	
145	This is the manifest's own spelling, read by whoever inspects `Cargo.toml` or `-V` output. It is not
146	a name for a step: a step is identified by its title, and an in-flight ladder rung carries neither a
147	number nor a version (see [Steps are named, not numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)).
148	The identifiers below count commits within a phase, and nothing dereferences one.
149	
150	- `X.Y.Z-0`: Preparation
151	- `X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, ...: the commits between
152	- `X.Y.Z`: Close-out (bare version, no suffix)
153	
154	**Preparation is optional.** A lightweight cycle, with no ladder and no setup commit, skips `-0` and
155	starts at `-1` (its first commit). A single-step cycle is one commit, the Close-out, and carries the
156	bare `X.Y.Z` ([Cycle shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)). The same holds at every level: a sub-cycle
157	needing no Preparation omits its `.0` (see Nesting). One that grows a Preparation later adds the `0`
158	step without renumbering siblings.

161

163	- `-1.0`: Preparation of the `-1` sub-cycle (final identifier `0`).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The closing's acceptance check for "feat: vc-x1 commit, install, and run-dev",
# run against the dev binary in a scratch dual workspace under tmp/accept.
# Each numbered section is one clause of the check as the record states it.
set -u
ROOT=/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/vc-x1
BIN=$ROOT/tmp/dev/bin/vc-x1
BASE=$ROOT/tmp/accept
rm -rf "$BASE"
mkdir -p "$BASE/home/.config/jj"
printf '[user]\nname = "accept"\nemail = "accept@example.com"\n' > "$BASE/home/.config/jj/config.toml"
export HOME=$BASE/home
export XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$BASE/home/.config
unset JJ_CONFIG
export PATH=$ROOT/tmp/dev/bin:$PATH

fails=0
ok()   { echo "OK   $1"; }
bad()  { echo "FAIL $1"; fails=$((fails+1)); }
# expect_ok NAME cmd...: the command must exit 0
expect_ok()  { local n=$1; shift; if "$@" > "$BASE/out.txt" 2>&1; then ok "$n"; else bad "$n (rc=$?)"; cat "$BASE/out.txt"; fi; }
# expect_err NAME cmd...: the command must exit non-zero
expect_err() { local n=$1; shift; if "$@" > "$BASE/out.txt" 2>&1; then bad "$n (exited 0)"; cat "$BASE/out.txt"; else ok "$n"; fi; }
# said PATTERN: the last command's output contains PATTERN (fixed string)
said() { if grep -qF -- "$1" "$BASE/out.txt"; then ok "  says: $1"; else bad "  does not say: $1"; cat "$BASE/out.txt"; fi; }
desc() { jj -R "$1" log --no-graph -r "$2" -T 'description' ; }
cid()  { jj -R "$1" log --no-graph -r "$2" -T 'change_id' ; }

echo "== 0 init a scratch dual workspace with local bare remotes"
cd "$BASE"
expect_ok "init" $BIN --no-banner init ./tr --repo "local=$BASE"
W=$BASE/tr
A=$W/.agent-session
cd "$W"
jj bookmark create cyc -r @- > /dev/null 2>&1 && ok "bookmark cyc at main" || bad "bookmark cyc"

echo "== 1 commit -s b makes a pair whose trailers name each other"
echo one > one.txt
echo 'journal 1' > "$A/journal.jsonl"
expect_ok "commit -s b rung one" $BIN --no-banner commit -s b --title "feat: one" --body "One."

## Dev artifact name

When other projects consume the built artifact (e.g. the installed CLI) while this repo is under
active development, the dev build installs under a separate name so a mid-cycle install never
clobbers the binary consumers are running:

- **Name**: the manifest's package name carries a `-dev` suffix (`<name>` -> `<name>-dev`). If Rust,
  `[package].name`, so the per-commit flow's `cargo install` produces `<name>-dev` and leaves plain
  `<name>` untouched.
- **Constant, not per-step**: the step already lives in the version-of-record (`<name>-dev -V`
  reports the exact rung). A per-step name would churn the manifest every commit and litter the
  install dir with stale binaries.
- **Promotion**: plain `<name>` updates only by an explicit act: a separate clone built at the
  chosen commit with the plain name (or a copy of the dev binary), never by the per-commit flow's
  install.

**Single-name variant**: a repo striving to release makes the package name the binary's name, plain
`<name>` on `main` only:

- **The opening renames**: its bump sets `<name>-dev` beside the suffixed version, and every rung
  and the closing build under the dev name, the closing over the bare version.
- **Land restores**: the rename back to `<name>` is Land's act, so the stable name is only ever
  installed from what `main` will carry.
- **A build script guards the pairing** on every cargo verb: a suffixed version under the stable
  name fails the build, so no mid-cycle install can clobber the consumers' binary.

  installed from what `main` will carry.

  name fails the build, so no mid-cycle install can clobber the consumers' binary.

# Commit model

Two commit bodies from the `config loader` cycle in [cycle-model.md](cycle-model.md), shown as
specimens rather than a skeleton: a work rung's body and a bookend's. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [Commit-body form](prose.md#commit-body-form).

## A work rung

Title: `refactor: split loader from parser`

```
Config loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load a
config without parsing it and a test cannot parse one without a file on
disk. The move into its own module is what forces the split.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config::loader` finds and reads the file and returns the text with
    its path, so a caller that only wants to know which file was read
    stops there.
  - `config::parser` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands
    it a string and never touches the filesystem.
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field
    access moves behind the module boundary and the CLI no longer knows
    the file's shape.
```

The intro states this commit's problem and defines "split", the word the title assumes. Each `*`
is one facet of it, each `-` under a `*` answers that facet, and nothing names a file that the
diff already lists.

## A bookend

Title: `refactor: extract config loader opening`

```
Opens the cycle "refactor: extract config loader". Its record is the

107	## vc-x1 push: what it does and does not do
108	
109	`vc-x1 push <bookmark> --yes --title "..." --body "..."` commits both repos with the approved title
110	and body (`--yes` because push's gates need a tty the agent sandbox lacks, and the user's approval
111	of the shown title and body already covers them), stamps each new commit's `ochid:` trailer
112	([above](#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)), pushes the work bookmark, and squash-pushes the agent
113	repo's `main`. Three behaviors to keep in mind:
114	
115	- **No checks of the project's own.** vc-x1 runs no build or tests. Validation is the per-rung
116	  flow's job, run *before* the push. The one check that remains is `push-work` verifying the
117	  bookmark's remote refs are tracked.
118	- **Rerunning is safe.** Push keeps no state and cannot resume: every stage no-ops when its work is
119	  already done, so a failed run is re-run, not resumed. If push exits after `push-work` but before
120	  the agent-repo publish, `vc-x1 squash-push -R <agent-dir>` by hand is the rest of it.
121	- **`ochid:` trailers are stamped by push** ([No hand-written
122	  trailers](#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)), never hand-written into `--title` or `--body`.
123	- **The agent-repo is a linear journal.**
124	  - One push is one agent-repo commit on its `main`, paired with the work-repo commit, whatever
125	    bookmark the work-repo is on.
126	  - Never create an agent-repo bookmark mirroring a work-repo one: it steers session pushes at
127	    the wrong remote ref.
128	- **Squash-push again if `@` is non-empty** after a pass.
129	  - The agent keeps writing session data while the command runs, so its own record lands after
130	    the squash.
131	  - Session data is append-only, so a re-run never conflicts.
132	  - A single pass is never guaranteed to leave `@` empty.
133	
134	A late work-repo tweak after the push (a forgotten edit) needs `jj squash --ignore-immutable` and a
135	re-push, which is a remote rewrite and takes approval like any push.

163	  committed change and publishes it in one invocation.
164	- Any other revision works as the `=<rev>` right-hand side. When `<rev>` is not `@-`, follow with
165	  `jj new <rev> -R .` so the working copy actually sits on the new line. Otherwise the bookmark
166	  exists and the next commit lands somewhere else.

174	closing words before the final invocation, silence after ([At
175	rest](../AGENTS.md#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push)):

178	   name](versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)): rename `<name>-dev` back to `<name>` in the manifest,
179	   `vc-x1 validate --fast` so the lockfile follows, and `jj squash` folds the edit into the closing
180	   (`@` sits directly above it).

187	   cycle anymore.

189	   `jj git push --bookmark <bookmark>` ([Bookmark per
190	   cycle](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)). The long-lived case below gets the same
191	   disposal once fully merged.

194	  of `main`, and the situation wants a look, not a flag.

226	## Close-out shapes
227	
228	The two shapes a ladder can land in, chosen by the user and recorded at close-out, executed at
229	[Land](#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land) ([Close-out](../AGENTS.md#close-out)). A single-step cycle
230	is one commit and lands as it is:
231	
232	- **trapezoid**, the current default: a merge commit whose first parent is the trunk and whose
233	  second is the ladder, so `git log --first-parent` reads one commit per cycle while every rung
234	  stays reachable. Reshaped at Land by the [recipe below](#trapezoid-close-out-recipe) and published
235	  by the landing fast-forward itself.
236	- **keep separate**, one commit per rung on `main`, when the decomposition itself is informative.
237	
238	Squash is not a shape: each rung's `ochid:` trailer is a change id, a squash keeps one and drops the
239	rest, and every agent-repo commit that pointed at a dropped rung is left dangling ([Cycle
240	shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).
241	
242	**Preview before choosing.** The cycle's net change is the tree diff from `<base>` to the tip,
243	whatever shape the commits between are in: `jj diff --from <base> --to <tip>`, or the gitk range
244	described in [Read a change in gitk at full context](#read-a-change-in-gitk-at-full-context). The
245	trapezoid keeps each rung reachable while `git log --first-parent` shows this net diff once landed,
246	and keep separate shows the rungs themselves. The choice is made on what `main` will carry.
247	
248	## Read a change in gitk at full context
249	
250	gitk renders a change three ways, and at full context each answers a different question. Raise
251	"Lines of context" to the longest file's length, or to a large number such as 1000 (`--context 1000`
252	is the CLI equivalent), to see the entire file, then select:
253	
254	- **New version**: the file as it now is, with the added lines lit. This is what the permanent
255	  branch will carry, so it is the view for judging whether a change reads as one thing.
256	- **Old version**: the file as it was, with the removed lines lit. It answers what the change costs,
257	  which a diff states only as minus lines out of context.
258	- **Diff**: the two interleaved. At full context it is the whole file with the edit marked in place,
259	  which is the reading a reviewer wants when the edit is small and the file is not.
260	
261	The above reads one commit at a time and is useful. Another mode is to see how several commits
262	together changed the tree since a given `<base>` commit. To do that:
263	
264	- Hover over the commit you want as the `<base>`, right click and select "Mark this commit".
265	- Hover over any commit above the `<base>`, right click and select "Diff marked commit -> this".
266	
267	Now New version, Old version and Diff show the net change of everything between `<base>` and `this`.
268	If `<base>` is the parent of the `opening` commit and `this` is the `closing`, that is the cycle's
269	net change, and it can help you decide what shape to choose ([Close-out shapes](#close-out-shapes)).
270	
271	## Trapezoid close-out recipe
272	
273	The reshape behind the trapezoid shape, run at [Land](#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land) step 2: the
274	close-out commit, pushed linearly by the closing rung, becomes a merge whose first parent is the
275	trunk line and whose second parent is the cycle's ladder. Nothing here publishes, the merge goes out
276	with Land's fast-forward.
277	
278	```
279	  main line   ...--<base>------------------<closeout>--
280	                      \                    /
281	  ladder             <rung-1>--...--<tip>-+
282	```
283	
284	- `<base>`: the **parent of the ladder's first rung**, the trunk position when the cycle opened. It
285	  becomes the first parent. Not always the previous close-out: a cycle landed linearly since
286	  (keep-separate shape, or a single-step cycle) sits on the trunk line and must stay there.
287	- `<tip>`: the cycle's last commit before the close-out. It becomes the second parent.
288	- `<closeout>`: the close-out commit, reshaped here.
289	
290	1. `jj rebase -r <closeout> --onto <base> --onto <tip>`: `<closeout>` becomes the merge. Parent
291	   order is the argument order.
292	2. `jj new <closeout>`: an empty `@` above the merge. The bookmark followed the rewrite on its own.
293	   What step 1 leaves misplaced is the working copy: `jj rebase -r` re-parents descendants onto the
294	   rebased commit's old parent, so the empty `@` lands beside the merge on `<tip>` and the tree
295	   reverts to pre-close-out content, which looks alarming and is not.
296	3. Verify two parents: `jj log -r <closeout> -T 'parents.map(|p| p.change_id().short(8))'` must list
297	   both. jj preserves the second parent even though `<base>` is an ancestor of `<tip>` (observed at
298	   three consecutive close-outs), but a collapsed merge is indistinguishable from a correct one in
299	   `jj log --no-graph`.
300	
301	Details:
302	
303	- **Trailers survive.** The restore's squash and the reshape change `<closeout>`'s SHA but not its
304	  change id, so the `ochid:` trailers stamped at the closing push stay valid in both directions.
305	- **Immutability.** No flag is needed: a topic bookmark's commits are not on `trunk()` until Land's
306	  fast-forward.
307	
308	Recovery:
309	
310	- **Nothing is published until Land's fast-forward**, so the whole reshape is undoable with
311	  `jj undo` / `jj op restore`.
312	- **A collapsed or mis-parented merge**: undo and redo step 1 with the corrected revisions. Do not
313	  land a shape you did not intend. After the fast-forward the remote boundary is crossed and
314	  recovery is forward-only.
315	- **Working copy left beside the merge** (step 2 skipped): `jj new <closeout>` after the fact. Any
316	  commit made in the meantime branches off `<tip>` and needs a rebase onto the merge.
